newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Average wheat yield per ha in Bulgaria rises.
newsitem.headline: Average wheat yield per ha in Bulgaria rises.

text.p: Bulgaria has harvested 693,540 tonnes of wheat from 17.2 percent of the sown area so far producing an average yield of 3.27 tonnes per hectare, higher than previously estimated two tonnes per hectare, farm ministry figures show.
"We have collected 693,540 tonnes of wheat from 211,813 hectares harvested so far and the average yield is 3.27 tonnes per hectare," agriculture ministry spokeswoman told reporters.
At this yield Bulgaria may collect around four million tonnes of wheat from a total of some 1.23 million hectares of wheat sown area.

But the farm ministry declined to make preliminary forecasts saying that it depended on how long the weather will remain dry long enough to let farmers harvest all of the crop. The yield also varied from one region to another.
In May Agriculture Minister Ventsislav Varbanov estimated this year's wheat crop at around 2.4 million tonnes and forecasts were based on an assumed average yield of two tonnes per hectare.
Varbanov said Bulgaria needed 1.072 million tonnes of bread and feed wheat to cover a consumption gap before the 1998 crop.

Bulgaria has collected 738,493 tonnes of barley from 246,893 harvested hectares out of a total 286,755 of barley sown last year. The farm ministry said expected barley crop will cover domestic consumption.
Bulgaria has to export some 232,000 tonnes of wheat this year under futures contracts agreed earlier this year to offset bread shortages.
The country's annual consumption is estimated at 1.6 million tonnes of bread wheat and 800,000 tonnes of feed wheat.
